beats.say: Your pod died overnight. Nobody noticed until a customer did.
A bare pod is a single point of failure. You need something that never sleeps.
beats.label: The gap
beats.head: A bare pod is one point of failure

beats.say: This port has three controllers: the Deployment, the Job, and the DaemonSet.
beats.label: Port 2 · Workloads

check.prompt: A node dies and takes two of your three pods. What does the Deployment do?
check.why: The Deployment keeps the number you asked for. It replaces the pods on another node.

beats.say: First: the controller you use most.
You say: I want three. A Deployment keeps three pods running.
beats.label: Deployment
beats.head: Keeps the number you asked for

beats.say: Delete a pod, or lose a node. A new pod appears in seconds.
beats.label: Self-healing
beats.head: A lost pod is replaced

check.prompt: A new version fails to start during a rollout. What happens to the old pods?
check.why: A rollout waits for a new pod to be ready before it removes an old one.

beats.say: Second: ship a new version with no downtime.
New pods start, one by one. An old pod leaves only when a new pod is ready.
beats.label: Rollout
beats.head: New in, then old out

beats.say: A bad release? One command takes you back to the last version.
beats.label: Rollback
beats.head: Undo in seconds

beats.say: Third: some work has an end.
A Job runs a pod until it succeeds. A CronJob starts a Job on a schedule.
beats.label: Batch
beats.head: Job: once. CronJob: on a schedule.

beats.say: A DaemonSet runs one copy on every node. Use it for log agents.
beats.label: DaemonSet
beats.head: One pod on every node

beats.say: Deployments heal and roll. Jobs finish. DaemonSets cover every node.
beats.label: Workloads

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
